  1369→    /// Validate all reference integrity across the model
  1370→    ///
  1371→    /// Checks:
  1372→    /// - Universe specifications reference valid SpecIds
  1373→    /// - Domain universe_id references valid UniverseIds
  1374→    /// - Domain covered_by references valid SpecIds
  1375→    /// - Domain subdomains references valid DomainIds
  1376→    /// - AdmissibleSet universe_id references valid UniverseIds
  1377→    /// - AdmissibleSet contradicts references valid SpecIds
  1378→    /// - Transform source/target universes reference valid UniverseIds
  1379→    ///
  1380→    /// Returns Ok(()) if all references are valid, or Err with details of invalid references
  1381→    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), String> {
  1382→        let mut errors = Vec::new();
  1383→
  1384→        // Collect all valid IDs for reference checking
  1385→        let valid_universe_ids: HashSet<String> = self.universes.keys()
  1386→            .map(|id| id.as_str().to_string())
  1387→            .collect();
  1388→
  1389→        let valid_spec_ids: HashSet<String> = self.admissible_sets.keys()
  1390→            .map(|id| id.as_str().to_string())
  1391→            .collect();
  1392→
  1393→        let valid_domain_ids: HashSet<String> = self.domains.keys()
  1394→            .map(|id| id.as_str().to_string())
  1395→            .collect();
  1396→
  1397→        // Validate Universe references
  1398→        for (universe_id, universe) in &self.universes {
  1399→            // Check that all specifications in the universe exist
  1400→            let invalid_specs = universe.specifications.check_integrity(&valid_spec_ids);
  1401→            if !invalid_specs.is_empty() {
  1402→                errors.push(format!(
  1403→                    "Universe {} references non-existent specifications: {:?}",
  1404→                    universe_id.as_str(),
  1405→                    invalid_specs
  1406→                ));
  1407→            }
  1408→        }
  1409→
  1410→        // Validate Domain references
  1411→        for (domain_id, domain) in &self.domains {
  1412→            // Check that universe_id exists (try meta first, fall back to old field)
  1413→            let universe_id_str = if let Some(meta) = &domain.meta {
  1414→                meta.get_str("universe_id").map(|s| s.as_str())
  1415→            } else {
  1416→                domain.universe_id.as_ref().map(|id| id.as_str())
  1417→            };
  1418→
  1419→            if let Some(uid_str) = universe_id_str {
  1420→                if !valid_universe_ids.contains(uid_str) {
  1421→                    errors.push(format!(
  1422→                        "Domain {} references non-existent universe: {}",
  1423→                        domain_id.as_str(),
  1424→                        uid_str
  1425→                    ));
  1426→                }
  1427→            }
  1428→
  1429→            // Check that all covered_by specs exist (try proof_data first, fall back to old field)
  1430→            let covered_by = if let Some(proof_data) = &domain.proof_data {
  1431→                Some(&proof_data.covered_by)
  1432→            } else {
  1433→                domain.covered_by.as_ref()
  1434→            };
  1435→
  1436→            if let Some(covered_by_set) = covered_by {
  1437→                let invalid_specs = covered_by_set.check_integrity(&valid_spec_ids);
  1438→                if !invalid_specs.is_empty() {
  1439→                    errors.push(format!(
  1440→                        "Domain {} references non-existent specifications in covered_by: {:?}",
  1441→                        domain_id.as_str(),
  1442→                        invalid_specs
  1443→                    ));
  1444→                }
  1445→            }
  1446→
  1447→            // Check that all subdomains exist (from meta)
  1448→            if let Some(meta) = &domain.meta {
  1449→                if let Some(subdomains_str) = meta.get_str("subdomains") {
  1450→                    // Note: This is a simplified check; actual subdomain validation would need proper parsing
  1451→                    // For now, skip subdomain validation for new structure
  1452→                }
  1453→            } else if let Some(subdomains) = &domain.subdomains {
  1454→                let invalid_domains = subdomains.check_integrity(&valid_domain_ids);
  1455→                if !invalid_domains.is_empty() {
  1456→                    errors.push(format!(
  1457→                        "Domain {} references non-existent subdomains: {:?}",
  1458→                        domain_id.as_str(),
  1459→                        invalid_domains
  1460→                    ));
  1461→                }
  1462→            }
  1463→        }
  1464→
  1465→        // Validate AdmissibleSet references
  1466→        for (spec_id, admissible_set) in &self.admissible_sets {
  1467→            // Check that universe_id exists (try meta first, fall back to old field)
  1468→            let universe_id_ref = if let Some(meta) = &admissible_set.meta {
  1469→                Some(&meta.universe_id)
  1470→            } else {
  1471→                admissible_set.universe_id.as_ref()
  1472→            };
  1473→
  1474→            if let Some(uid) = universe_id_ref {
  1475→                if !valid_universe_ids.contains(uid.as_str()) {
  1476→                    errors.push(format!(
  1477→                        "AdmissibleSet {} references non-existent universe: {}",
  1478→                        spec_id.as_str(),
  1479→                        uid.as_str()
  1480→                    ));
  1481→                }
  1482→            }
  1483→
  1484→            // Check that all contradicts references exist (try proof_data first, fall back to old field)
  1485→            let contradicts = if let Some(proof_data) = &admissible_set.proof_data {
  1486→                Some(&proof_data.contradicts)
  1487→            } else {
  1488→                admissible_set.contradicts.as_ref()
  1489→            };
  1490→
  1491→            if let Some(contradicts_set) = contradicts {
  1492→                let invalid_contradicts = contradicts_set.check_integrity(&valid_spec_ids);
  1493→                if !invalid_contradicts.is_empty() {
  1494→                    errors.push(format!(
  1495→                        "AdmissibleSet {} references non-existent specifications in contradicts: {:?}",
  1496→                        spec_id.as_str(),
  1497→                        invalid_contradicts
  1498→                    ));
  1499→                }
  1500→            }
  1501→        }
  1502→
  1503→        // Validate Transform references
  1504→        for (transform_id, transform) in &self.transforms {
  1505→            // Check that source_universe exists

  1511→                ));
  1512→            }
  1513→
  1514→            // Check that target_universe exists
  1515→            if !valid_universe_ids.contains(transform.target_universe.as_str()) {

  1518→                    transform_id.as_str(),

  1520→                ));
  1521→            }
  1522→        }
  1523→
  1524→        if errors.is_empty() {

   590→
   591→        // Check if specs are explicitly marked as contradicting
   592→        let a_contradicts_b = if let Some(proof_data) = &spec_a.proof_data {
   593→            proof_data.contradicts.contains(&spec_b.spec_id)
   594→        } else if let Some(contradicts) = &spec_a.contradicts {
   595→            contradicts.contains(&spec_b.spec_id)
   596→        } else {
   597→            false
   598→        };
   599→
   600→        if a_contradicts_b {
   601→            steps.push(ProofStep {
   602→                description: "Specifications explicitly contradict each other".to_string(),
   603→                justification: "Explicit contradiction marker".to_string(),
   604→            });
   605→            return (ProofStatus::Refuted, steps);
   606→        }
   607→
   608→        // Basic heuristic checks
   609→        let contradictory = self.detect_obvious_contradiction(constraints_a, constraints_b);
   610→
   611→        if contradictory {
   612→            steps.push(ProofStep {
   613→                description: "Detected obvious contradiction in constraints".to_string(),
   614→                justification: "Constraint conflict analysis".to_string(),
   615→            });
   616→            (ProofStatus::Refuted, steps)
   617→        } else {
   618→            steps.push(ProofStep {
   619→                description: "No obvious contradiction detected".to_string(),
   620→                justification: "Heuristic constraint analysis".to_string(),
   621→            });
   622→            steps.push(ProofStep {
   623→                description: "Note: This is not a complete proof. SMT solver integration needed for soundness.".to_string(),
   624→                justification: "Limitation acknowledgment".to_string(),
   625→            });
   626→            (ProofStatus::Unknown, steps)
   627→        }
   628→    }

   630→    /// Check satisfiability via constraint analysis
   631→    fn check_satisfiability_via_constraints(
   632→        &self,
   633→        spec: &crate::udaf::AdmissibleSet,
   634→    ) -> (ProofStatus, Vec<ProofStep>) {
   635→        let mut steps = Vec::new();
   636→
   637→        // Get constraints from new structure first, fall back to old structure
   638→        let constraints = if let Some(proof_data) = &spec.proof_data {
   639→            &proof_data.constraints
   640→        } else if let Some(constraints) = &spec.constraints {
   641→            constraints
   642→        } else {
   643→            &vec![]
   644→        };
   645→
   646→        if constraints.is_empty() {
   647→            steps.push(ProofStep {
   648→                description: "No constraints - specification is trivially satisfiable".to_string(),
   649→                justification: "Empty constraint set".to_string(),
   650→            });
   651→            return (ProofStatus::Proven, steps);
   652→        }
   653→
   654→        steps.push(ProofStep {
   655→            description: format!("Analyzing {} constraints", constraints.len()),
   656→            justification: "Constraint enumeration".to_string(),
   657→        });
   658→
   659→        // Basic satisfiability check
   660→        let unsatisfiable = self.detect_obvious_unsatisfiability(constraints);
   661→
   662→        if unsatisfiable {
   663→            steps.push(ProofStep {
   664→                description: "Detected obvious unsatisfiability".to_string(),
   665→                justification: "Constraint conflict analysis".to_string(),
   666→            });
   667→            (ProofStatus::Refuted, steps)
   668→        } else {
   669→            steps.push(ProofStep {
   670→                description: "No obvious unsatisfiability detected".to_string(),
   671→                justification: "Heuristic constraint analysis".to_string(),
   672→            });
   673→            steps.push(ProofStep {
   674→                description: "Note: This is not a complete proof. SMT solver integration needed for soundness.".to_string(),
   675→                justification: "Limitation acknowledgment".to_string(),
   676→            });
   677→            (ProofStatus::Unknown, steps)
   678→        }
   679→    }

   681→    /// Extract description from constraint (tries new structure first, falls back to old)
   682→    fn get_constraint_description<'a>(&self, constraint: &'a crate::udaf::Constraint) -> &'a str {
   683→        if let Some(meta) = &constraint.meta {
   684→            if let Some(desc) = meta.get_str("description") {
   685→                return desc;
   686→            }
   687→        }
   688→        if let Some(desc) = &constraint.description {
   689→            return desc;
   690→        }
   691→        ""
   692→    }

   694→    /// Detect obvious contradictions between constraint sets
   695→    fn detect_obvious_contradiction(
   696→        &self,
   697→        constraints_a: &[crate::udaf::Constraint],
   698→        constraints_b: &[crate::udaf::Constraint],
   699→    ) -> bool {
   700→        // Check for explicit conflicts in numeric constraints
   701→        // e.g., "x >= 10" vs "x <= 5"
   702→
   703→        for a in constraints_a {
   704→            for b in constraints_b {
   705→                let desc_a = self.get_constraint_description(a);
   706→                let desc_b = self.get_constraint_description(b);
   707→                if self.constraints_conflict(desc_a, desc_b) {
   708→                    return true;
   709→                }
   710→            }
   711→        }
   712→
   713→        false
   714→    }
   715→
   716→    /// Detect obvious unsatisfiability within a constraint set
   717→    fn detect_obvious_unsatisfiability(
   718→        &self,
   719→        constraints: &[crate::udaf::Constraint],
   720→    ) -> bool {
   721→        // Check for internal conflicts
   722→        // e.g., "x >= 10" and "x <= 5" in the same spec
   723→
   724→        for i in 0..constraints.len() {
   725→            for j in (i+1)..constraints.len() {
   726→                let desc_i = self.get_constraint_description(&constraints[i]);
   727→                let desc_j = self.get_constraint_description(&constraints[j]);
   728→                if self.constraints_conflict(desc_i, desc_j) {
   729→                    return true;
   730→                }
   731→            }
   732→        }
   733→
   734→        false
   735→    }
   736→
   737→    /// Heuristic check if two constraints conflict
   738→    fn constraints_conflict(&self, desc_a: &str, desc_b: &str) -> bool {
   739→        let a_lower = desc_a.to_lowercase();
   740→        let b_lower = desc_b.to_lowercase();
   741→
   742→        // Numeric conflict patterns
   743→        // "at least X" vs "at most Y" where X > Y
   744→        if let (Some(min_a), Some(max_b)) = (
   745→            self.extract_minimum(&a_lower),
   746→            self.extract_maximum(&b_lower),
   747→        ) {
   748→            if min_a > max_b {
   749→                return true;
   750→            }
   751→        }
   752→
   753→        if let (Some(max_a), Some(min_b)) = (
   754→            self.extract_maximum(&a_lower),
   755→            self.extract_minimum(&b_lower),
   756→        ) {
   757→            if max_a < min_b {
   758→                return true;
   759→            }
   760→        }
   761→
   762→        // Boolean conflict patterns
   763→        // "must be X" vs "must not be X" / "forbidden X"
   764→        if (a_lower.contains("must be") || a_lower.contains("required"))
   765→            && (b_lower.contains("must not") || b_lower.contains("forbidden") || b_lower.contains("prohibited"))
   766→        {
   767→            // Check if they're about the same thing
   768→            let a_words: Vec<&str> = a_lower.split_whitespace().collect();
   769→            let b_words: Vec<&str> = b_lower.split_whitespace().collect();
   770→            let common_words: Vec<&str> = a_words.iter().filter(|w| b_words.contains(w)).copied().collect();
   771→
   772→            if common_words.len() >= 2 {
   773→                return true;
   774→            }
   775→        }
   776→
   777→        false
   778→    }
   779→
   780→    /// Extract minimum value from constraint description
   781→    fn extract_minimum(&self, desc: &str) -> Option<i64> {
   782→        // "at least N", "minimum N", ">= N"
   783→        if let Some(pos) = desc.find("at least") {
   784→            return self.extract_number(&desc[pos..]);
   785→        }
   786→        if let Some(pos) = desc.find("minimum") {
   787→            return self.extract_number(&desc[pos..]);
   788→        }
   789→        if let Some(pos) = desc.find(">=") {
   790→            return self.extract_number(&desc[pos..]);
   791→        }
   792→        None
   793→    }
   794→
   795→    /// Extract maximum value from constraint description
   796→    fn extract_maximum(&self, desc: &str) -> Option<i64> {
   797→        // "at most N", "maximum N", "<= N"
   798→        if let Some(pos) = desc.find("at most") {
   799→            return self.extract_number(&desc[pos..]);
   800→        }
   801→        if let Some(pos) = desc.find("maximum") {
   802→            return self.extract_number(&desc[pos..]);
   803→        }
   804→        if let Some(pos) = desc.find("<=") {
   805→            return self.extract_number(&desc[pos..]);
   806→        }
   807→        None
   808→    }
   809→
   810→    /// Extract first number from string
   811→    fn extract_number(&self, s: &str) -> Option<i64> {
   812→        for word in s.split_whitespace() {
   813→            if let Ok(n) = word.trim_matches(|c: char| !c.is_numeric()).parse::<i64>() {
   814→                return Some(n);
   815→            }
   816→        }
   817→        None
   818→    }

   830→    /// Get proofs for a specific specification
   831→    pub fn get_proofs_for_spec(&self, spec_id: &str) -> Vec<&Proof> {
   832→        self.proofs.values().filter(|p| {
   833→            match &p.property {
   834→                Property::Consistency { spec_a, spec_b } => {
   835→                    spec_a == spec_id || spec_b == spec_id
   836→                }
   837→                Property::Satisfiability { spec } => spec == spec_id,
   838→                Property::Implication { antecedent, consequent } => {
   839→                    antecedent == spec_id || consequent == spec_id
   840→                }
   841→                Property::Completeness { spec, .. } => spec == spec_id,
   842→                Property::TransformSoundness { source, target, .. } => {
   843→                    source == spec_id || target == spec_id
   844→                }
   845→            }
   846→        }).collect()
   847→    }

   849→    /// Heuristically detect underspecification (漏れA)
   850→    ///
   851→    /// Returns confidence-scored report, not a formal proof.
   852→    /// Underspecification is a design choice, not an error, so it cannot be formally proven wrong.
   853→    pub fn detect_underspecification(
   854→        &self,
   855→        spec: &crate::udaf::AdmissibleSet,
   856→        domain: &crate::udaf::Domain,
   857→        _universe: &crate::udaf::Universe,
   858→    ) -> UnderspecificationReport {
   859→        let mut confidence = 0.0f32;
   860→        let mut reasons = Vec::new();
   861→        let mut suggestions = Vec::new();
   862→
   863→        // Get constraints
   864→        let spec_constraints = if let Some(proof_data) = &spec.proof_data {
   865→            &proof_data.constraints
   866→        } else if let Some(constraints) = &spec.constraints {
   867→            constraints
   868→        } else {
   869→            &vec![]
   870→        };
   871→
   872→        let domain_constraints = if let Some(proof_data) = &domain.proof_data {
   873→            &proof_data.constraints
   874→        } else {
   875→            &vec![]
   876→        };
   877→
   878→        // Heuristic 1: Constraint count
   879→        // If spec has very few constraints relative to domain complexity
   880→        if spec_constraints.is_empty() {
   881→            confidence += 0.8;
   882→            reasons.push("Specification has no constraints".to_string());
   883→            suggestions.push("Add constraints to define the admissible set".to_string());
   884→        } else if spec_constraints.len() < 3 && !domain_constraints.is_empty() && domain_constraints.len() > spec_constraints.len() * 2 {
   885→            confidence += 0.4;
   886→            reasons.push(format!(
   887→                "Specification has only {} constraints, but domain has {} constraints",
   888→                spec_constraints.len(),
   889→                domain_constraints.len()
   890→            ));
   891→            suggestions.push("Consider adding more constraints to narrow the admissible set".to_string());
   892→        }
   893→
   894→        // Heuristic 2: Free variables
   895→        // Extract variable names from domain and spec
   896→        let domain_vars = self.extract_variable_names_from_constraints(domain_constraints);
   897→        let spec_vars = self.extract_variable_names_from_constraints(spec_constraints);
   898→
   899→        let unconstrained_vars: Vec<_> = domain_vars.iter()
   900→            .filter(|v| !spec_vars.contains(*v))
   901→            .collect();
   902→
   903→        if !unconstrained_vars.is_empty() {
   904→            confidence += 0.3 * (unconstrained_vars.len() as f32 / domain_vars.len().max(1) as f32);
   905→            reasons.push(format!(
   906→                "Domain mentions {} variable(s) not constrained in spec: {:?}",
   907→                unconstrained_vars.len(),
   908→                unconstrained_vars
   909→            ));
   910→            suggestions.push("Add constraints for unconstrained variables".to_string());
   911→        }
   912→
   913→        // Heuristic 3: Keyword matching
   914→        // Check if domain description mentions aspects not addressed in spec
   915→        let domain_desc = if let Some(meta) = &domain.meta {
   916→            meta.get_str("description").map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or("")
   917→        } else if let Some(desc) = &domain.description {
   918→            desc.as_str()
   919→        } else {
   920→            ""
   921→        };
   922→
   923→        let keywords = vec!["security", "performance", "reliability", "availability", "scalability"];
   924→        let domain_lower = domain_desc.to_lowercase();
   925→        let spec_text = spec_constraints.iter()
   926→            .filter_map(|c| {
   927→                if let Some(meta) = &c.meta {
   928→                    meta.get_str("description").map(|s| s.to_lowercase())
   929→                } else {
   930→                    c.description.as_ref().map(|s| s.to_lowercase())
   931→                }
   932→            })
   933→            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
   934→            .join(" ");
   935→
   936→        for keyword in keywords {
   937→            if domain_lower.contains(keyword) && !spec_text.contains(keyword) {
   938→                confidence += 0.1;
   939→                reasons.push(format!(
   940→                    "Domain mentions '{}' but specification does not address it",
   941→                    keyword
   942→                ));
   943→                suggestions.push(format!("Add constraints related to {}", keyword));
   944→            }
   945→        }
   946→
   947→        // Heuristic 4: Constraint tightness
   948→        // Check if constraints are very loose (wide ranges, weak requirements)
   949→        let loose_constraints = spec_constraints.iter().filter(|c| {
   950→            let desc = if let Some(meta) = &c.meta {
   951→                meta.get_str("description").map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or("")
   952→            } else {
   953→                c.description.as_deref().unwrap_or("")
   954→            };
   955→            let lower = desc.to_lowercase();
   956→            // Very loose patterns: "at least 1", "at most 1000000", etc.
   957→            (lower.contains("at least 1") && !lower.contains("at least 10")) ||
   958→            lower.contains("at most 1000") ||
   959→            lower.contains("any") ||
   960→            lower.contains("optional")
   961→        }).count();
   962→
   963→        if loose_constraints > 0 {
   964→            confidence += 0.2 * (loose_constraints as f32 / spec_constraints.len().max(1) as f32);
   965→            reasons.push(format!(
   966→                "{} constraint(s) appear very loose or permissive",
   967→                loose_constraints
   968→            ));
   969→            suggestions.push("Consider tightening loose constraints".to_string());
   970→        }
   971→
   972→        // Cap confidence at 1.0
   973→        confidence = confidence.min(1.0);
   974→
   975→        let is_likely_underspecified = confidence >= 0.5;
   976→
   977→        UnderspecificationReport {
   978→            spec_id: spec.spec_id.as_str().to_string(),
   979→            domain_id: domain.id.as_str().to_string(),
   980→            is_likely_underspecified,
   981→            confidence,
   982→            reasons,
   983→            suggestions,
   984→        }
   985→    }

   987→    /// Extract variable names from constraints
   988→    fn extract_variable_names_from_constraints(&self, constraints: &[crate::udaf::Constraint]) -> std::collections::HashSet<String> {
   989→        let mut vars = std::collections::HashSet::new();
   990→        for constraint in constraints {
   991→            let desc = if let Some(meta) = &constraint.meta {
   992→                meta.get_str("description").map(|s| s.as_str()).unwrap_or("")
   993→            } else {
   994→                constraint.description.as_deref().unwrap_or("")
   995→            };
   996→
   997→            // Extract variable name (heuristic: word before "must", "should", "is", etc.)
   998→            let words: Vec<&str> = desc.split_whitespace().collect();
   999→            for (i, &word) in words.iter().enumerate() {
  1000→                if word == "must" || word == "should" || word == "is" {
  1001→                    if i > 0 {
  1002→                        vars.insert(words[i-1].to_lowercase().trim_matches(|c: char| !c.is_alphanumeric()).to_string());
  1003→                    }
  1004→                }
  1005→            }
  1006→        }
  1007→        vars
  1008→    }
  1009→}

# Refactoring Plan: Reorganize spec-core/src into formal/ Directory

## Executive Summary

This plan outlines a comprehensive refactoring to reorganize the spec-core/src directory by moving all UDAF and Prover code into a new `formal/` directory structure. The refactoring will split large files (>500 LOC) into focused modules while maintaining backward compatibility and following Rust best practices.

**Goal**: Create a clean, maintainable structure that organizes formal verification components (UDAF model + Prover) separately from extraction/graph infrastructure.

---

## Current State Analysis

### Large Files Requiring Splitting

1. **udaf.rs** - 1,536 LOC
   - Universe (52 lines, lines 29-84)
   - Domain (74 lines + 38 lines DomainProofData, lines 87-250)
   - AdmissibleSet (55 lines + 48 lines ProofData + 37 lines Metadata, lines 252-411)
   - Constraint (35 lines, lines 413-463)
   - TransformFunction (92 lines, lines 465-585)
   - UDAFModel (794 lines including serde helpers, lines 587-1536)
   
2. **prover/mod.rs** - 1,238 LOC
   - Proof (21 lines, lines 20-42)
   - Property (21 lines, lines 44-66)
   - ProofMethod (30 lines, lines 68-99)
   - ProofStatus (8 lines, lines 101-115)
   - ProofStep (8 lines, lines 117-125)
   - Prover (884 lines, lines 127-1009)
   - UnderspecificationReport (15 lines, lines 1011-1023)
   - Tests (215 lines, lines 1032-1238)

3. **prover/z3_backend.rs** - 965 LOC
   - Z3Backend struct and implementation (entire file)
   - Tests (146 lines, lines 819-965)

### Existing Submodules

- **udaf/ids.rs** - 392 LOC (well-sized, move as-is)
- **udaf/metadata.rs** - 525 LOC (slightly large but cohesive, move as-is)
- **udaf/refs.rs** - 388 LOC (well-sized, move as-is)

### Files Staying Outside formal/

- **graph.rs** - 2,783 LOC (SpecGraph, analysis, metrics)
- **extract.rs** - 1,622 LOC (RustExtractor, ProtoExtractor, etc.)
- **store.rs** - 7,556 bytes (~250 LOC, FileStore, DirectoryStore)
- **ai_semantic.rs** - 6,220 bytes (~200 LOC, AI integration)

---

## Target Directory Structure

```
formal/
  mod.rs              # Formal layer entry point (NEW)
  udaf/
    mod.rs            # UDAF module entry (NEW)
    universe.rs       # Universe type (~60 LOC) (NEW)
    domain.rs         # Domain + DomainProofData (~120 LOC) (NEW)
    admissible_set.rs # AdmissibleSet + ProofData + Metadata (~150 LOC) (NEW)
    constraint.rs     # Constraint + ConstraintKind (~40 LOC) (NEW)
    transform.rs      # TransformFunction + Strategy + Kind (~150 LOC) (NEW)
    model.rs          # UDAFModel orchestrator (~850 LOC) (NEW)
    ids.rs            # IDs (MOVE from udaf/)
    metadata.rs       # Metadata (MOVE from udaf/)
    refs.rs           # Reference sets (MOVE from udaf/)
  prover/
    mod.rs            # Prover module entry (NEW)
    types.rs          # Proof, Property, ProofStatus, ProofStep, ProofMethod (~100 LOC) (NEW)
    prover.rs         # Prover core implementation (~900 LOC) (NEW)
    z3_backend.rs     # Z3Backend (MOVE from prover/)
```

---

## Detailed File Breakdown

### 1. formal/mod.rs (NEW)

**Purpose**: Entry point for the formal layer, re-exports all public types.

**Content**:
```rust
//! Formal verification layer for specORACLE
//! 
//! This module contains the UDAF (Universe/Domain/AdmissibleSet/Function) model
//! and the Prover for formal verification.

pub mod udaf;
pub mod prover;

// Re-export commonly used types
pub use udaf::{
    UDAFModel, Universe, Domain, AdmissibleSet, TransformFunction,
    TransformStrategy, Constraint, ConstraintKind, TransformKind,
    UniverseId, DomainId, SpecId, TransformId, IdError,
    MetadataKey, Metadata, UniverseMetadata, DomainMetadata,
    ConstraintMetadata, TransformMetadata,
    SpecSet, DomainSet,
};

pub use prover::{
    Prover, Proof, Property, ProofMethod, ProofStatus, ProofStep,
    UnderspecificationReport,
};
```

**Visibility**: All items are `pub` for external access.

**Dependencies**: None (re-exports only).

**Estimated LOC**: ~30

---

### 2. formal/udaf/mod.rs (NEW)

**Purpose**: UDAF module entry point, declares submodules and re-exports types.

**Content**:
```rust
//! U/D/A/f Model: Theoretical foundation of specORACLE
//! 
//! Based on conversation.md and motivation.md:
//! - U (Universe): The space in which specifications are defined
//! - D (Domain): The region that specifications actually cover
//! - A (Admissible set): The set of allowed implementations
//! - f (Transform function): Mappings between universes

mod ids;
mod metadata;
mod refs;
mod universe;
mod domain;
mod admissible_set;
mod constraint;
mod transform;
mod model;

pub use transform::{TransformFunction, TransformKind, TransformStrategy};

- Easy to rollback to last working state

- Clear separation: formal layer vs. extraction/graph layer

- Easier to navigate for new contributors

- Easier to explain architecture to new users

2. **Improve documentation** with examples in each module
3. **Add benchmarks** for UDAFModel operations

   - Extract source file finding logic (~30 LOC)
5. **Add property-based tests** for UDAF invariants
6. **Create a formal/README.md** explaining the theoretical foundation

These are the 5 most critical files to understand before implementing this plan:

1. **src/udaf.rs** (1,536 LOC)
   - Reason: Source of all UDAF types to be split
   - Contains: All core types, serde helpers, UDAFModel implementation

2. **src/prover/mod.rs** (1,238 LOC)
   - Reason: Source of all Prover types to be split
   - Contains: Proof types, Prover implementation, tests
   - Action: Will be split into types.rs and prover.rs

   - Action: Critical to maintain backward compatibility

4. **src/graph.rs** (2,783 LOC)

   - Action: Update imports to use formal::udaf::*

   - Reason: Largest new file, orchestrates all UDAF components
   - Contains: UDAFModel, construct_u0(), serde helpers
   - Action: Core of the refactored structure, needs careful extraction

## Conclusion

This refactoring plan provides a comprehensive, step-by-step approach to reorganizing spec-core/src into a clean formal/ directory structure. The migration is designed to be:

- **Safe**: Each phase is verifiable, easy to rollback
- **Incremental**: No "big bang" rewrite, build always works

The result will be a more maintainable, scalable codebase that clearly separates formal verification concerns (UDAF + Prover) from extraction and graph infrastructure.

# Refactoring Plan: Reorganize spec-core into formal/ Directory

## Context

The user requested to refactor the spec-core codebase by:
1. Creating `spec-core/src/formal/` directory (already exists but empty)
2. Moving UDAF and Prover code under this formal layer
3. Splitting overly large files (some >1000 LOC) into smaller, focused modules
4. Following Rust best practices for module organization

### Current Problems

**Large Files:**
- `udaf.rs` - 1,536 LOC (Universe, Domain, AdmissibleSet, Constraint, TransformFunction, UDAFModel)
- `prover/mod.rs` - 1,238 LOC (Proof types, Prover implementation, tests)
- `prover/z3_backend.rs` - 965 LOC (Z3 integration)

**Scattered Organization:**
- UDAF types in `src/udaf.rs` and `src/udaf/` submodule
- Prover types in `src/prover/`
- No clear "formal verification" layer despite having formal/ directory

### Solution: Formal Layer Reorganization

Move all formal verification code (UDAF model + Prover) into `formal/` with proper module structure:
- Split large files into focused modules (<500 LOC each)
- Maintain backward compatibility through lib.rs re-exports
- Follow Rust conventions (inline tests, clear module hierarchy)

---

## Target Directory Structure

```
formal/
  mod.rs              # Formal layer entry point (~30 LOC)
  udaf/
    mod.rs            # UDAF module entry (~50 LOC)
    universe.rs       # Universe type (~60 LOC)
    domain.rs         # Domain + DomainProofData (~120 LOC)
    admissible_set.rs # AdmissibleSet + metadata (~150 LOC)
    constraint.rs     # Constraint + ConstraintKind (~40 LOC)
    transform.rs      # TransformFunction (~150 LOC)
    model.rs          # UDAFModel orchestrator (~850 LOC)
    ids.rs            # Type-safe IDs (move from udaf/, 392 LOC)
    metadata.rs       # Metadata system (move from udaf/, 525 LOC)
    refs.rs           # Reference sets (move from udaf/, 388 LOC)
  prover/
    mod.rs            # Prover module entry (~20 LOC)
    types.rs          # Proof, Property, ProofStatus, etc. (~100 LOC)
    prover.rs         # Prover implementation + tests (~900 LOC)
    z3_backend.rs     # Z3 integration (move, 965 LOC)
```

---

## File Breakdown

### formal/mod.rs (NEW, ~30 LOC)

Entry point for formal verification layer. Re-exports all public types from udaf and prover modules.

```rust
//! Formal verification layer for specORACLE
pub mod udaf;
pub mod prover;

// Re-export commonly used types
pub use udaf::{UDAFModel, Universe, Domain, AdmissibleSet, ...};
pub use prover::{Prover, Proof, Property, ProofStatus, ...};
```

### formal/udaf/mod.rs (NEW, ~50 LOC)

UDAF module entry. Re-exports all public types from submodules.

### formal/udaf/universe.rs (NEW, ~60 LOC)

**Extract from:** `src/udaf.rs` lines 29-84

**Types:** `Universe` struct + impl (root(), projection(), layer())

**Dependencies:** ids::UniverseId, refs::SpecSet, metadata::UniverseMetadata

### formal/udaf/domain.rs (NEW, ~120 LOC)

**Extract from:** `src/udaf.rs` lines 87-250

**Types:** `Domain`, `DomainProofData` + impls

**Dependencies:** ids::{DomainId, UniverseId}, refs::{SpecSet, DomainSet}, constraint::Constraint

### formal/udaf/admissible_set.rs (NEW, ~150 LOC)

**Extract from:** `src/udaf.rs` lines 252-411

**Types:** `AdmissibleSet`, `AdmissibleSetProofData`, `AdmissibleSetMetadata` + impls

**Dependencies:** ids::SpecId, refs::SpecSet, constraint::Constraint

### formal/udaf/constraint.rs (NEW, ~40 LOC)

**Extract from:** `src/udaf.rs` lines 413-463

**Types:** `Constraint`, `ConstraintKind`

**Dependencies:** metadata::ConstraintMetadata

### formal/udaf/transform.rs (NEW, ~150 LOC)

**Extract from:** `src/udaf.rs` lines 465-585

**Types:** `TransformFunction`, `TransformKind`, `TransformStrategy` + impls

**Dependencies:** ids::{TransformId, UniverseId}, metadata::TransformMetadata

### formal/udaf/model.rs (NEW, ~850 LOC)

**Extract from:** `src/udaf.rs` lines 587-1536

**Types:** `UDAFModel` + serde helper modules + impl

**Note:** Keep all serde helpers (lines 613-739) here - they're tightly coupled to UDAFModel

**Dependencies:** All other udaf types, crate::{SpecGraph, RustExtractor, InferredSpecification, NodeKind, EdgeKind}

### formal/udaf/{ids,metadata,refs}.rs (MOVE)

**Action:** Move unchanged from `src/udaf/` to `src/formal/udaf/`
- ids.rs (392 LOC) - Type-safe IDs
- metadata.rs (525 LOC) - Metadata system
- refs.rs (388 LOC) - Reference sets

**Changes:** None (already use correct relative imports)

### formal/prover/mod.rs (NEW, ~20 LOC)

Prover module entry. Re-exports public types.

```rust
pub mod types;
pub mod prover;
mod z3_backend;  // Internal

pub use types::{Proof, Property, ProofMethod, ProofStatus, ProofStep};
pub use prover::{Prover, UnderspecificationReport};
```

### formal/prover/types.rs (NEW, ~100 LOC)

**Extract from:** `src/prover/mod.rs` lines 20-125

**Types:** `Proof`, `Property`, `ProofMethod`, `ProofStatus`, `ProofStep`

**Dependencies:** serde, std::collections::HashMap

### formal/prover/prover.rs (NEW, ~900 LOC)

**Extract from:** `src/prover/mod.rs` lines 127-1238

**Types:** `Prover`, `UnderspecificationReport` + impls + tests

**Dependencies:** super::types::*, super::z3_backend::Z3Backend, crate::formal::udaf::*

**Tests:** Keep inline (lines 1032-1238), update imports to use `crate::formal::udaf::*`

### formal/prover/z3_backend.rs (MOVE, 965 LOC)

**Action:** Move from `src/prover/z3_backend.rs` to `src/formal/prover/z3_backend.rs`

**Import updates:**
```rust
// OLD:
use crate::udaf::{Constraint, ConstraintKind};
use crate::prover::{ProofStatus, ProofStep};

// NEW:
use crate::formal::udaf::{Constraint, ConstraintKind};
use super::types::{ProofStatus, ProofStep};
```

---

## Migration Sequence

### Phase 1: Setup (5 min)

Verify `formal/udaf/` and `formal/prover/` directories exist (created earlier):
```bash
ls -la src/formal/
```

### Phase 2: UDAF Migration (2 hours)

**Step 1:** Copy existing submodules
```bash
cp src/udaf/ids.rs src/formal/udaf/
cp src/udaf/metadata.rs src/formal/udaf/
cp src/udaf/refs.rs src/formal/udaf/
```

**Step 2-7:** Create new files by extracting from udaf.rs:
- constraint.rs (lines 413-463)
- universe.rs (lines 29-84)
- domain.rs (lines 87-250)
- admissible_set.rs (lines 252-411)
- transform.rs (lines 465-585)
- model.rs (lines 587-1536)

**Step 8:** Create `formal/udaf/mod.rs` with re-exports

**Verify:** `cargo check --all-features` (old files still exist, should work)

### Phase 3: Prover Migration (1 hour)

**Step 1:** Create types.rs (extract lines 20-125 from prover/mod.rs)

**Step 2:** Copy z3_backend.rs and update imports

**Step 3:** Create prover.rs (extract lines 127-1238, update test imports)

**Step 4:** Create `formal/prover/mod.rs`

**Verify:** `cargo check --all-features`

### Phase 4: Create formal/mod.rs (15 min)

Create `formal/mod.rs` with re-exports of all public types

**Verify:** `cargo check --all-features`

### Phase 5: Update lib.rs (15 min)

Update module declarations and re-exports:
```rust
// OLD:
pub mod udaf;
pub mod prover;

// NEW:
pub mod formal;
pub use formal::udaf::{...};
pub use formal::prover::{...};
```

**Verify:** `cargo check --all-features` should PASS

### Phase 6: Update Dependent Files (1 hour)

Update imports in files that use udaf/prover:

**Files to update:**
- `src/graph.rs` - Change `use crate::udaf::*` to `use crate::formal::udaf::*`
- `src/extract.rs` - Check and update if needed
- `src/store.rs` - Check and update if needed
- `src/ai_semantic.rs` - Check and update if needed

**Verify:** `cargo check --all-features` must PASS

### Phase 7: Cleanup (10 min)

Remove old files:
```bash
rm src/udaf.rs
rm -rf src/udaf/
rm -rf src/prover/
```

**Verify:** `cargo check --all-features && cargo test --all-features`

### Phase 8: Final Verification (30 min)

```bash
cargo test --all-features
cargo test --no-default-features
cargo clippy --all-features
cargo fmt --check
cargo doc --all-features --no-deps
```

---

## Critical Files

**Source files to split:**
1. `src/udaf.rs` (1,536 LOC) - Extract Universe, Domain, AdmissibleSet, Constraint, TransformFunction, UDAFModel
2. `src/prover/mod.rs` (1,238 LOC) - Extract Proof types, Prover implementation

**Files to move:**
3. `src/udaf/ids.rs` → `src/formal/udaf/ids.rs`
4. `src/udaf/metadata.rs` → `src/formal/udaf/metadata.rs`
5. `src/udaf/refs.rs` → `src/formal/udaf/refs.rs`
6. `src/prover/z3_backend.rs` → `src/formal/prover/z3_backend.rs`

**Files to update imports:**
7. `src/lib.rs` - Public API, must maintain backward compatibility
8. `src/graph.rs` - Major consumer, needs `use crate::formal::udaf::*`
9. `src/extract.rs` - Check for udaf imports
10. `src/store.rs` - Check for udaf imports

---

## Backward Compatibility

**Public API unchanged:** lib.rs re-exports maintain exact same paths:
- `spec_core::UDAFModel` still works
- `spec_core::Prover` still works
- All public types accessible from crate root

**Internal reorganization only:** External crates won't break.

---

## Rollback Strategy

- **Before Phase 7:** Revert new files and lib.rs changes
- **After Phase 7:** `git checkout HEAD -- src/udaf.rs src/udaf/ src/prover/`
- **Commit each phase** for easy rollback

---

## Verification Checklist

After each phase:
- [ ] `cargo check --all-features` passes
- [ ] `cargo check --no-default-features` passes
- [ ] No unused import warnings
- [ ] No dead code warnings

After Phase 8:
- [ ] All tests pass (with and without z3-solver)
- [ ] Clippy has no warnings
- [ ] Formatting is correct
- [ ] Documentation builds
- [ ] Public API unchanged

---

## Expected Outcome

**Benefits:**
- Clear formal verification layer (`formal/`)
- Smaller, focused modules (<500 LOC)
- Better maintainability and discoverability
- Follows Rust module best practices
- Full backward compatibility

**Estimated effort:** 5-6 hours
**Risk level:** Low (incremental, verifiable, easy rollback)

# Refactoring Plan: Reorganize spec-core into formal/ Directory

## Context

The user requested to refactor the spec-core codebase by:
1. Creating `spec-core/src/formal/` directory (already exists but empty)
2. Moving UDAF and Prover code under this formal layer
3. Splitting overly large files (some >1000 LOC) into smaller, focused modules
4. Following Rust best practices for module organization

### Current Problems

**Large Files:**
- `udaf.rs` - 1,536 LOC (Universe, Domain, AdmissibleSet, Constraint, TransformFunction, UDAFModel)
- `prover/mod.rs` - 1,238 LOC (Proof types, Prover implementation, tests)
- `prover/z3_backend.rs` - 965 LOC (Z3 integration)

**Scattered Organization:**
- UDAF types in `src/udaf.rs` and `src/udaf/` submodule
- Prover types in `src/prover/`
- No clear "formal verification" layer despite having formal/ directory

### Solution: Formal Layer Reorganization

Move all formal verification code (UDAF model + Prover) into `formal/` with proper module structure:

- Maintain backward compatibility through lib.rs re-exports

# Implementation Plan: UDA Model Minimization + Proof Mechanisms

## Context

### Problem 1: UDA Model is Not Minimized

Current UDAF structures mix three concerns without clear separation:
1. **Identity** (IDs for entity identification)
2. **Proof-essential data** (constraints, relationships needed for formal verification)
3. **Metadata** (human-readable names, descriptions, organizational info)

**Analysis shows**:
- **Universe**: NO proof-essential fields (only organizational)
- **Domain**: `covered_by` is proof-essential; `name`, `description` are metadata
- **AdmissibleSet**: `constraints`, `contradicts` are proof-essential; `name`, `universe_id` are metadata
- **Prover currently accesses metadata unnecessarily** - should only see IDs + proof data

### Problem 2: Prover Doesn't Use D and U Properly

The current Prover implementation only uses AdmissibleSet (A) for proofs, completely ignoring Domain (D) and Universe (U). This violates the theoretical foundation of the UDA/f model:

- **Contradiction proofs** currently check `A1 ∩ A2 ≠ ∅` but should check `A1 ∩ A2 ∩ D ≠ ∅` (within domain)
- **Leak detection** requires U (for leak A) and D (for leak B) but these are not used
- **仕様はAの要素であり、Dがなければ定まらない** - specification cannot be determined without D

The user has confirmed that while the broad concept is correct, we need to determine:
1. Can these proofs actually be implemented?
2. How should they be implemented?

### Investigation Results

**Technical Feasibility:**
- ✅ **Implication (A1 ⊆ A2)**: Fully feasible with current Z3 infrastructure
- ⚠️ **Completeness (D ⊆ D_S)**: Feasible IF Domain is formalized as constraints
- ⚠️ **Underspecification (leak A)**: Only heuristically detectable (not formally provable)
- ❌ **TransformSoundness**: Not feasible with current architecture (deferred)

**Core Challenge:**
- D (Domain) is currently only a natural language description, not a formal set
- U (Universe) has no formal boundary definition, only organizational structure
- **Key insight**: 漏れA（未規定）は設計上の選択であり、証明不可能。ヒューリスティック検出のみ可能。

## Solution: Two-Phase Refactoring

### Phase A: Minimize UDA Model (3-Layer Separation)
### Phase B: Implement Proof Mechanisms Using Minimized Model

---

## Phase A: UDA Model Minimization

### Design: Composition-Based 3-Layer Structure

Each UDAF entity (Universe, Domain, AdmissibleSet) is restructured into:
1. **Identifier field** (ID only)
2. **ProofData struct** (only proof-essential fields)
3. **Metadata struct** (everything else)

**Benefits**:
- Clear separation of concerns at struct level
- Prover can accept only `&ProofData`, never metadata
- Compile-time enforcement of layer boundaries
- Minimal migration impact (composition, not replacement)

### New Structure Definitions

#### Universe (Minimized)

**Current** (spec-core/src/udaf.rs:36-52):

    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,

    pub metadata: UniverseMetadata,

```

**New**:
```rust
pub struct Universe {
    // Layer 1: Identifier
    pub id: UniverseId,

    // Layer 2: Proof Data - NONE (Universe has no proof-essential data)
    // (Universe is purely organizational)

    // Layer 3: Metadata
    pub meta: UniverseMetadata,
}

pub struct UniverseMetadata {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub specifications: SpecSet,  // Organizational, not proof-relevant
    pub extra: HashMap<String, String>,  // Extensible metadata

```

#### Domain (Minimized)

```

**New**:
```rust
pub struct Domain {

    pub id: DomainId,

    // Layer 2: Proof Data
    pub proof_data: DomainProofData,

    // Layer 3: Metadata
    pub meta: DomainMetadata,
}

pub struct DomainProofData {
    pub constraints: Vec<Constraint>,  // NEW: Formal domain boundaries
    pub covered_by: SpecSet,           // For completeness: D ⊆ D_S
}

pub struct DomainMetadata {
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub universe_id: UniverseId,      // Organizational
    pub subdomains: DomainSet,        // Organizational hierarchy
    pub extra: HashMap<String, String>,
}
```

#### AdmissibleSet (Minimized)

**Current** (spec-core/src/udaf.rs:156-173):
```rust

    pub spec_id: SpecId,
    pub universe_id: UniverseId,
    pub constraints: Vec<Constraint>,
    pub contradicts: SpecSet,
    pub metadata: Metadata,
}
```

**New**:
```rust
pub struct AdmissibleSet {
    // Layer 1: Identifier
    pub id: SpecId,

    // Layer 2: Proof Data
    pub proof_data: AdmissibleSetProofData,

    // Layer 3: Metadata
    pub meta: AdmissibleSetMetadata,
}

    pub constraints: Vec<Constraint>,
    pub contradicts: SpecSet,  // Pre-marked contradictions
}

pub struct AdmissibleSetMetadata {
    pub universe_id: UniverseId,  // Organizational
    pub extra: HashMap<String, String>,

```

#### Constraint (Minimized)

**Current** (spec-core/src/udaf.rs:208-222):
```rust

    pub description: String,
    pub formal: Option<String>,
    pub kind: ConstraintKind,
    pub metadata: ConstraintMetadata,

**New**:
```rust
pub struct Constraint {
    // Layer 2: Proof Data (no identifier needed for constraints)
    pub formal: Option<String>,   // SMT formula (primary proof representation)
    pub kind: ConstraintKind,     // Universal, Existential, etc.

    // Layer 3: Metadata
    pub meta: ConstraintMetadata,
}

pub struct ConstraintMetadata {
    pub description: String,      // Human-readable (NOT used in proofs)
    pub pattern: Option<String>,  // Matched pattern (e.g., "at_least")
    pub source: Option<String>,   // Original source text
    pub extra: HashMap<String, String>,
}
```

**Critical Change**: `Constraint.description` moves to metadata. Proofs use `Constraint.formal` only.
- If `formal` is None, extract from `meta.description` during proof preparation
- Prover never directly accesses `meta.description`

### Migration Strategy

**Step 1: Add new fields alongside old ones**

```rust
pub struct Domain {
    // OLD (deprecated)
    pub id: DomainId,
    pub name: String,
    pub description: String,
    pub universe_id: UniverseId,
    pub covered_by: SpecSet,
    pub subdomains: DomainSet,
    pub metadata: DomainMetadata,

    // NEW (preferred)
    pub proof_data: Option<DomainProofData>,  // Populated gradually
    pub meta: Option<DomainMetadata>,         // Populated gradually
}
```

**Step 2: Dual population** - populate both old and new during transition

**Step 3: Update consumers one by one**:
1. Prover → use `proof_data` only
2. CLI display → use `meta` only
3. Serialization → support both formats

**Step 4: Remove old fields** once all consumers migrated

### Prover Integration After Minimization

**Before** (current):
```rust

    &mut self,
    spec_a: &AdmissibleSet,  // Has metadata mixed in
    spec_b: &AdmissibleSet,

```

**After** (minimized):

pub fn prove_consistency(
    &mut self,
    spec_a_id: &SpecId,
    spec_a_proof: &AdmissibleSetProofData,  // ONLY proof data
    spec_b_id: &SpecId,
    spec_b_proof: &AdmissibleSetProofData,
) -> Proof
```

Prover **cannot compile** if it tries to access metadata - type safety enforced.

---

## Phase B: Implement Proof Mechanisms

(Using minimized UDA model from Phase A)

## Approach: Hybrid Formalization

### 1. Domain Formalization (Already in Phase A)

**Domain.proof_data.constraints** added in Phase A minimization:
```rust
pub struct DomainProofData {
    pub constraints: Vec<Constraint>,  // Formal domain boundaries
    pub covered_by: SpecSet,
}
```

**Rationale**: Hybrid approach allows:
- Optional formalization: `constraints` can be empty
- Graceful degradation when D not formalized (falls back to A-only proofs)
- Progressive enhancement as specifications mature
- Clear separation: constraints in proof_data, description in metadata

### 2. Three Categories of Proof Implementation

#### Category A: Formal Proofs (Z3-based) ✅

**1. Implication: A1 ⊆ A2**
- Formula: `UNSAT(A1 ∧ ¬A2)`
- Interpretation: Every implementation satisfying A1 also satisfies A2
- Implementation: `prove_implication(A1, A2) -> Proof`
- Status: **Highly feasible** - works with current Z3Backend

**2. Consistency Within Domain: A1 ∩ A2 ∩ D ≠ ∅**
- Formula: `SAT(A1 ∧ A2 ∧ D)`
- Interpretation: Specifications are consistent within the domain
- Implementation: `prove_consistency_within_domain(A1, A2, D) -> Proof`
- Graceful degradation: If `D.constraints.is_empty()`, falls back to current `prove_consistency(A1, A2)`

**3. Completeness: D ⊆ D_S**
- Formula: `UNSAT(D ∧ ¬(A1 ∨ A2 ∨ ... ∨ An))`
- Interpretation: Every element of domain is covered by some specification
- Implementation: `prove_completeness(D, [A1, A2, ...An]) -> Proof`
- Detects **漏れB（カバレッジ不足）**
- Requires: D must be formalized

#### Category B: Heuristic Analysis ⚠️

**4. Underspecification Detection (Leak A)**
- **Cannot be formally proven** - underspecification is a design choice, not an error
- Heuristics: constraint count, free variables, domain keyword matching
- Implementation: `detect_underspecification(A, D, U) -> UnderspecificationReport`
- Returns: Confidence score (0.0-1.0), reasons, suggestions
- Detects **漏れA（未規定）**

#### Category C: Future Work ❌

**5. TransformSoundness: f(A_source) ⊆ A_target**
- Requires formal semantics of transform functions
- Current architecture uses opaque strategy patterns (ASTAnalysis, NLPInference, etc.)
- Not feasible without major architectural changes
- **Explicitly deferred to future work**

    // A1: "x >= 5", A2: "x >= 10"
    // Expect: Refuted (counterexample: x=7)
}

#[test]
fn prove_consistency_within_domain() {
    // A1: "password >= 8", A2: "password <= 20", D: "1 <= password <= 100"
    // Expect: Proven (consistent within domain)
}

#[test]

    // D.constraints.is_empty()
    // Expect: Falls back to prove_consistency, adds note to proof steps
}

    // D: "1 <= x <= 10", Specs: ["x >= 1", "x <= 10"]
    // Expect: Proven
}

#[test]

    // D: "1 <= x <= 10", Specs: ["x >= 1 and x < 5"]
    // Expect: Refuted (witness: x=7)

# Prove implication
spec prover implication spec-strict spec-loose
```

## Key Decisions & Rationale

### Why Optional Domain.constraints?

**Decision**: Make Domain.constraints optional (empty Vec by default)

**Rationale**:
- Many domains are defined informally (natural language only)
- Forcing formalization would be impractical
- Graceful degradation allows system to work at all maturity levels
- Progressive enhancement: users can formalize domains as specs mature

### Why Not Prove Underspecification?

**Decision**: Underspecification detection is heuristic, not a formal proof

**Rationale**:
- 漏れA（未規定）は設計上の選択であり、エラーではない
- "Too wide" is subjective - depends on intended design space
- Cannot formally define "correct width" of admissible set
- Heuristics provide useful guidance without false certainty

### Why Defer TransformSoundness?

**Decision**: Explicitly defer TransformSoundness to future work

**Rationale**:
- Requires formal semantics of transform functions
- Current architecture uses opaque strategies (ASTAnalysis, NLPInference)
- Would need major architectural changes (symbolic execution, program synthesis)
- Not critical for core UDA-based proof mechanisms

## Expected Outcomes

### Phase 1 Deliverables

- ✅ Domain.constraints field added
- ✅ Implication proof implemented
- ✅ Consistency-within-domain proof implemented
- ✅ Graceful degradation when D not formalized

### Phase 2 Deliverables

- ✅ Completeness proof (detects 漏れB)
- ✅ Underspecification heuristics (detects 漏れA)
- ✅ CLI integration

### Success Criteria

**Technical Success**:
1. Proofs correctly use U, D, A according to UDA/f theory
2. Z3 formal verification works when constraints encodable
3. Graceful degradation when formal constraints unavailable
4. No regression in existing prove_consistency/prove_satisfiability

**Theoretical Success**:
1. 矛盾の証明 uses D and A (not just A)
2. 漏れB検出 uses D (coverage gap detection)
3. 漏れA検出 uses U heuristically (underspecification hints)
4. Acknowledges fundamental limitations (Gödel, Rice's theorem)

## Limitations Acknowledged

### What We CAN Do
- ✅ Formal proofs for satisfiability, consistency, implication
- ✅ Coverage gap detection (when D formalized)
- ✅ Heuristic underspecification analysis

### What We CANNOT Do (Fundamental Limits)
- ❌ Prove underspecification is "wrong" (it's a design choice)
- ❌ Measure infinite set sizes (|A|, |D|, |U|)
- ❌ Prove universal properties without bounded domains
- ❌ Verify transform soundness without formal semantics

### Graceful Degradation
- D not formalized → Fall back to A-only proofs, note in proof steps
- Z3 returns Unknown → Report uncertainty honestly
- Constraints not encodable → Skip with warning, suggest manual review

# Refactoring Plan: Reorganize spec-core into formal/ Directory

## Context

The user requested to refactor the spec-core codebase by:
1. Creating `spec-core/src/formal/` directory (already exists but empty)
2. Moving UDAF and Prover code under this formal layer
3. Splitting overly large files (some >1000 LOC) into smaller, focused modules
4. Following Rust best practices for module organization

### Current Problems

**Large Files:**
- `udaf.rs` - 1,536 LOC (Universe, Domain, AdmissibleSet, Constraint, TransformFunction, UDAFModel)

# Refactoring Plan: Reorganize spec-core into formal/ Directory

## Context

The user requested to refactor the spec-core codebase by:
1. Creating `spec-core/src/formal/` directory (already exists but empty)
2. Moving UDAF and Prover code under this formal layer
3. Splitting overly large files (some >1000 LOC) into smaller, focused modules
4. Following Rust best practices for module organization

### Current Problems

**Large Files:**
- `udaf.rs` - 1,536 LOC (Universe, Domain, AdmissibleSet, Constraint, TransformFunction, UDAFModel)
- `prover/mod.rs` - 1,238 LOC (Proof types, Prover implementation, tests)
- `prover/z3_backend.rs` - 965 LOC (Z3 integration)

**Scattered Organization:**
- UDAF types in `src/udaf.rs` and `src/udaf/` submodule
- Prover types in `src/prover/`
- No clear "formal verification" layer despite having formal/ directory

### Solution: Formal Layer Reorganization

Move all formal verification code (UDAF model + Prover) into `formal/` with proper module structure:
- Split large files into focused modules (<500 LOC each)
- Maintain backward compatibility through lib.rs re-exports
- Follow Rust conventions (inline tests, clear module hierarchy)

`formal/` IS the UDA/f model space itself. No `udaf/` subdirectory needed.

# Refactoring Plan: Reorganize spec-core into formal/ Directory

## Context

The user requested to refactor the spec-core codebase by:
1. Creating `spec-core/src/formal/` directory (already exists but empty)
2. Moving UDAF and Prover code under this formal layer
3. Splitting overly large files (some >1000 LOC) into smaller, focused modules
4. Following Rust best practices for module organization

### Current Problems

**Large Files:**
- `udaf.rs` - 1,536 LOC (Universe, Domain, AdmissibleSet, Constraint, TransformFunction, UDAFModel)
- `prover/mod.rs` - 1,238 LOC (Proof types, Prover implementation, tests)
- `prover/z3_backend.rs` - 965 LOC (Z3 integration)

**Scattered Organization:**
- UDAF types in `src/udaf.rs` and `src/udaf/` submodule
- Prover types in `src/prover/`
- No clear "formal verification" layer despite having formal/ directory

### Solution: Formal Layer Reorganization

Move all formal verification code (UDAF model + Prover) into `formal/` with proper module structure:
- Split large files into focused modules (<500 LOC each)
- Maintain backward compatibility through lib.rs re-exports
- Follow Rust conventions (inline tests, clear module hierarchy)

---

`formal/` IS the UDA/f model space itself. No `udaf/` subdirectory needed.

```

- UDAF types in `src/udaf.rs` and `src/udaf/` submodule
- Prover types in `src/prover/`
- No clear "formal verification" layer despite having formal/ directory

Move all formal verification code (UDAF model + Prover) into `formal/` with proper module structure:

- Maintain backward compatibility through lib.rs re-exports
- Follow Rust conventions (inline tests, clear module hierarchy)

---

`formal/` represents the UDA/f formal space. Each concept gets its own directory with ID type included.

```
formal/

  universe/                 # U (Universe)
    mod.rs                  # Re-exports
    universe.rs             # Universe type (~60 LOC)
    universe_id.rs          # UniverseId type (~40 LOC)
    universe_metadata.rs    # UniverseMetadata (~100 LOC)

    mod.rs                  # Re-exports
    domain.rs               # Domain + DomainProofData (~120 LOC)
    domain_id.rs            # DomainId type (~40 LOC)
    domain_metadata.rs      # DomainMetadata (~100 LOC)
    domain_set.rs           # DomainSet (reference collection, ~80 LOC)

  admissible_set/           # A (Admissible Set)
    mod.rs                  # Re-exports
    admissible_set.rs       # AdmissibleSet + ProofData (~150 LOC)
    spec_id.rs              # SpecId type (~40 LOC)
    spec_set.rs             # SpecSet (reference collection, ~80 LOC)
    admissible_set_metadata.rs  # Metadata (~80 LOC)

  constraint/
    mod.rs                  # Re-exports
    constraint.rs           # Constraint + ConstraintKind (~40 LOC)
    constraint_metadata.rs  # ConstraintMetadata (~100 LOC)

  transform/                # f (Transform Functions)
    mod.rs                  # Re-exports
    transform.rs            # TransformFunction (~150 LOC)
    transform_id.rs         # TransformId type (~40 LOC)
    transform_metadata.rs   # TransformMetadata (~100 LOC)

    mod.rs                  # Re-exports
    model.rs                # UDAFModel core (~600 LOC)
    populate.rs             # populate_from_graph (~250 LOC)
    serde_helpers.rs        # Serialization helpers (~150 LOC)

  metadata/                 # Shared metadata infrastructure

    prover.rs               # Prover implementation (~600 LOC)
    underspec.rs            # Underspecification detection (~200 LOC)
    z3_backend.rs           # Z3 integration (965 LOC)
```

**Rationale:**
- Each UDA/f concept (U/D/A/f) has its own directory
- ID types live with their corresponding model (UniverseId with Universe)
- Metadata types organized by concept
- model/ contains orchestration logic split into focused files
- Clear separation between model structure and proof mechanisms

---

## File Breakdown

input.content:
# Refactoring Plan: Reorganize spec-core into formal/ Directory

## Context

The user requested to refactor spec-core by:
1. Moving all code into `spec-core/src/formal/` (formal verification layer)
2. Splitting large files (udaf.rs: 1,536 LOC, prover/mod.rs: 1,238 LOC) into smaller modules
3. Following Rust best practices with clear directory structure
4. **Key insight**: `formal/` IS the UDA/f space itself, not a wrapper around `udaf/`
5. **Important**: Each concept (U/D/A/f) should have its own directory with ID types included

### Current Problems

- udaf.rs (1,536 LOC) - too large, mixes all UDA/f concepts
- prover/mod.rs (1,238 LOC) - too large, mixes proof types and implementation
- IDs are separated in udaf/ids.rs instead of living with their models
- Metadata scattered across files
- No clear conceptual organization

---

## Target Directory Structure

Each UDA/f concept gets its own directory. ID types live with their models.

```
formal/
  mod.rs                        # Entry point, re-exports

  universe/                     # U (Universe)
    mod.rs
    universe.rs                 # Universe type
    universe_id.rs              # UniverseId
    universe_metadata.rs        # UniverseMetadata

  domain/                       # D (Domain)
    mod.rs
    domain.rs                   # Domain + DomainProofData
    domain_id.rs                # DomainId
    domain_metadata.rs          # DomainMetadata
    domain_set.rs               # DomainSet reference collection

  admissible_set/               # A (Admissible Set)
    mod.rs
    admissible_set.rs           # AdmissibleSet + ProofData
    spec_id.rs                  # SpecId
    spec_set.rs                 # SpecSet reference collection
    admissible_set_metadata.rs  # Metadata

  constraint/
    mod.rs
    constraint.rs               # Constraint + ConstraintKind
    constraint_metadata.rs      # ConstraintMetadata

  transform/                    # f (Transform Functions)
    mod.rs
    transform.rs                # TransformFunction + Kind + Strategy
    transform_id.rs             # TransformId
    transform_metadata.rs       # TransformMetadata

  model/                        # UDAFModel orchestrator
    mod.rs
    model.rs                    # Core UDAFModel struct + methods
    populate.rs                 # populate_from_graph logic
    serde_helpers.rs            # Serialization helpers

  metadata/                     # Shared metadata infrastructure
    mod.rs
    metadata_key.rs             # MetadataKey enum
    metadata.rs                 # Base Metadata type

  proof/                        # Proof mechanisms
    mod.rs
    types.rs                    # Proof, Property, ProofStatus, etc.
    prover.rs                   # Prover implementation
    underspec.rs                # Underspecification detection
    z3_backend.rs               # Z3 integration
```

---

## Migration Strategy

### Phase 1: Create Directory Structure

```bash
cd spec-core/src/formal
mkdir -p universe domain admissible_set constraint transform model metadata proof
```

### Phase 2: Extract and Split Universe

Extract from `src/udaf.rs` lines 29-84 (Universe) and `src/udaf/ids.rs` (UniverseId):

- `formal/universe/universe.rs` - Universe type
- `formal/universe/universe_id.rs` - UniverseId from ids.rs
- `formal/universe/universe_metadata.rs` - From udaf/metadata.rs
- `formal/universe/mod.rs` - Re-exports

### Phase 3: Extract and Split Domain

Extract from `src/udaf.rs` lines 87-250 (Domain):

- `formal/domain/domain.rs` - Domain + DomainProofData
- `formal/domain/domain_id.rs` - DomainId from ids.rs
- `formal/domain/domain_set.rs` - From udaf/refs.rs
- `formal/domain/domain_metadata.rs` - From udaf/metadata.rs
- `formal/domain/mod.rs` - Re-exports

### Phase 4: Extract and Split AdmissibleSet

Extract from `src/udaf.rs` lines 252-411:

- `formal/admissible_set/admissible_set.rs` - AdmissibleSet + ProofData
- `formal/admissible_set/spec_id.rs` - SpecId from ids.rs
- `formal/admissible_set/spec_set.rs` - From udaf/refs.rs
- `formal/admissible_set/admissible_set_metadata.rs` - From udaf/metadata.rs
- `formal/admissible_set/mod.rs` - Re-exports

### Phase 5: Extract and Split Constraint

Extract from `src/udaf.rs` lines 413-463:

- `formal/constraint/constraint.rs` - Constraint + ConstraintKind
- `formal/constraint/constraint_metadata.rs` - From udaf/metadata.rs
- `formal/constraint/mod.rs` - Re-exports

### Phase 6: Extract and Split Transform

Extract from `src/udaf.rs` lines 465-585:

- `formal/transform/transform.rs` - TransformFunction + Kind + Strategy
- `formal/transform/transform_id.rs` - TransformId from ids.rs
- `formal/transform/transform_metadata.rs` - From udaf/metadata.rs
- `formal/transform/mod.rs` - Re-exports

### Phase 7: Extract and Split UDAFModel

Extract from `src/udaf.rs` lines 587-1536:

- `formal/model/model.rs` - UDAFModel struct + core methods (~600 LOC)
- `formal/model/populate.rs` - populate_from_graph logic (~250 LOC)
- `formal/model/serde_helpers.rs` - Serde helper modules (~150 LOC)
- `formal/model/mod.rs` - Re-exports

### Phase 8: Create Metadata Module

Extract shared metadata infrastructure:

- `formal/metadata/metadata_key.rs` - MetadataKey enum
- `formal/metadata/metadata.rs` - Base Metadata type
- `formal/metadata/mod.rs` - Re-exports

### Phase 9: Extract and Split Prover

- `formal/proof/underspec.rs` - detect_underspecification + UnderspecificationReport (~200 LOC)

- `formal/proof/mod.rs` - Re-exports

### Phase 10: Create formal/mod.rs

Create top-level module with re-exports of all public types.

### Phase 11: Update lib.rs

```rust
// OLD:
pub mod udaf;
pub mod prover;

// NEW:
pub mod formal;
pub use formal::{
    Universe, UniverseId, Domain, DomainId, AdmissibleSet, SpecId,
    Constraint, TransformFunction, TransformId, UDAFModel,
    Prover, Proof, Property, ProofStatus,
    // ... all public types
};
```

### Phase 12: Update Dependent Files

Update imports in:
- `src/graph.rs` - `use crate::udaf::*` → `use crate::formal::*`
- `src/extract.rs` - Check and update
- `src/store.rs` - Check and update

### Phase 13: Remove Old Files

```bash
rm src/udaf.rs
rm -rf src/udaf/
rm -rf src/prover/
```

### Phase 14: Verify

```bash
cargo test --all-features
cargo clippy --all-features
cargo fmt --check
```

---

## Critical Files to Modify

**Source files to split:**
1. `src/udaf.rs` (1,536 LOC) → Split into universe/, domain/, admissible_set/, constraint/, transform/, model/
2. `src/udaf/ids.rs` (392 LOC) → Split UniverseId, DomainId, SpecId, TransformId into respective directories
3. `src/udaf/metadata.rs` (525 LOC) → Split into respective *_metadata.rs files
4. `src/udaf/refs.rs` (388 LOC) → Split SpecSet, DomainSet into respective directories
5. `src/prover/mod.rs` (1,238 LOC) → Split into proof/{types.rs, prover.rs, underspec.rs}
6. `src/prover/z3_backend.rs` (965 LOC) → Move to formal/proof/z3_backend.rs

**Files to update:**
7. `src/lib.rs` - Module declarations and re-exports
8. `src/graph.rs` - Import paths
9. `src/extract.rs` - Import paths (if any)
10. `src/store.rs` - Import paths (if any)

---

## Key Import Pattern Changes

**Old structure:**
```rust
use crate::udaf::{Universe, Domain, AdmissibleSet, Constraint, UDAFModel};
use crate::udaf::ids::{UniverseId, DomainId, SpecId};
use crate::prover::{Prover, Proof};
```

**New structure:**
```rust
use crate::formal::{
    Universe, UniverseId,
    Domain, DomainId,
    AdmissibleSet, SpecId,
    Constraint,
    UDAFModel,
    Prover, Proof,
};
```

---

## Backward Compatibility

**Public API unchanged via lib.rs re-exports:**
- `spec_core::Universe` still works
- `spec_core::UDAFModel` still works
- `spec_core::Prover` still works
- All types accessible from crate root

External crates won't break.

---

## Verification Checklist

After each phase:
- [ ] `cargo check --all-features` passes
- [ ] No unused import warnings

After Phase 14:
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Clippy has no warnings
- [ ] Documentation builds
- [ ] Public API unchanged

---

## Expected Outcome

**Benefits:**
- Clear directory organization by concept (U/D/A/f)
- ID types live with their models (not centralized)
- Smaller, focused files (<300 LOC each)
- Better discoverability and maintainability
- Follows Rust module best practices

**Estimated effort:** 6-8 hours
**Risk level:** Low (incremental, verifiable)

## Context

The user requested to refactor spec-core by:
1. Moving all code into `spec-core/src/formal/` (formal verification layer)
2. Splitting large files (udaf.rs: 1,536 LOC, prover/mod.rs: 1,238 LOC) into smaller modules
3. Following Rust best practices with clear directory structure

Each UDA/f concept gets its own directory. ID types live with their models.

# Refactoring Plan: Reorganize spec-core into formal/ Directory

## Context

The user requested to refactor the spec-core codebase by:
1. Creating `spec-core/src/formal/` directory (already exists but empty)
2. Moving UDAF and Prover code under this formal layer
3. Splitting overly large files (some >1000 LOC) into smaller, focused modules
4. Following Rust best practices for module organization

### Current Problems

**Large Files:**
- `udaf.rs` - 1,536 LOC (Universe, Domain, AdmissibleSet, Constraint, TransformFunction, UDAFModel)
- `prover/mod.rs` - 1,238 LOC (Proof types, Prover implementation, tests)
- `prover/z3_backend.rs` - 965 LOC (Z3 integration)

**Scattered Organization:**
- UDAF types in `src/udaf.rs` and `src/udaf/` submodule
- Prover types in `src/prover/`
- No clear "formal verification" layer despite having formal/ directory

### Solution: Formal Layer Reorganization

Move all formal verification code (UDAF model + Prover) into `formal/` with proper module structure:
- Split large files into focused modules (<500 LOC each)
- Maintain backward compatibility through lib.rs re-exports
- Follow Rust conventions (inline tests, clear module hierarchy)

---

## Target Directory Structure

`formal/` represents the UDA/f formal space. Each concept gets its own directory with ID type included.

```
formal/
  mod.rs                    # UDA/f formal space entry point

  universe/                 # U (Universe)
    mod.rs                  # Re-exports
    universe.rs             # Universe type (~60 LOC)
    universe_id.rs          # UniverseId type (~40 LOC)
    universe_metadata.rs    # UniverseMetadata (~100 LOC)

  domain/                   # D (Domain)
    mod.rs                  # Re-exports
    domain.rs               # Domain + DomainProofData (~120 LOC)
    domain_id.rs            # DomainId type (~40 LOC)
    domain_metadata.rs      # DomainMetadata (~100 LOC)
    domain_set.rs           # DomainSet (reference collection, ~80 LOC)

  admissible_set/           # A (Admissible Set)
    mod.rs                  # Re-exports
    admissible_set.rs       # AdmissibleSet + ProofData (~150 LOC)
    spec_id.rs              # SpecId type (~40 LOC)
    spec_set.rs             # SpecSet (reference collection, ~80 LOC)
    admissible_set_metadata.rs  # Metadata (~80 LOC)

  constraint/
    mod.rs                  # Re-exports
    constraint.rs           # Constraint + ConstraintKind (~40 LOC)
    constraint_metadata.rs  # ConstraintMetadata (~100 LOC)

  transform/                # f (Transform Functions)
    mod.rs                  # Re-exports
    transform.rs            # TransformFunction (~150 LOC)
    transform_id.rs         # TransformId type (~40 LOC)
    transform_metadata.rs   # TransformMetadata (~100 LOC)

  model/                    # UDAFModel orchestrator
    mod.rs                  # Re-exports
    model.rs                # UDAFModel core (~600 LOC)
    populate.rs             # populate_from_graph (~250 LOC)
    serde_helpers.rs        # Serialization helpers (~150 LOC)

  metadata/                 # Shared metadata infrastructure
    mod.rs                  # Re-exports
    metadata_key.rs         # MetadataKey enum (~50 LOC)
    metadata.rs             # Base Metadata type (~80 LOC)

  proof/                    # Proof mechanisms
    mod.rs                  # Re-exports
    types.rs                # Proof, Property, ProofStatus (~100 LOC)
    prover.rs               # Prover implementation (~600 LOC)
    underspec.rs            # Underspecification detection (~200 LOC)
    z3_backend.rs           # Z3 integration (965 LOC)
```

**Rationale:**
- Each UDA/f concept (U/D/A/f) has its own directory
- ID types live with their corresponding model (UniverseId with Universe)
- Metadata types organized by concept
- model/ contains orchestration logic split into focused files
- Clear separation between model structure and proof mechanisms

---

# Refactoring Plan: Reorganize spec-core into formal/ Directory

## Context

The user requested to refactor spec-core by:
1. Moving all code into `spec-core/src/formal/` (formal verification layer)
2. Splitting large files (udaf.rs: 1,536 LOC, prover/mod.rs: 1,238 LOC) into smaller modules
3. Following Rust best practices with clear directory structure
4. **Key insight**: `formal/` IS the UDA/f space itself, not a wrapper around `udaf/`
5. **Important**: Each concept (U/D/A/f) should have its own directory with ID types included

### Current Problems

- udaf.rs (1,536 LOC) - too large, mixes all UDA/f concepts
- prover/mod.rs (1,238 LOC) - too large, mixes proof types and implementation
- IDs are separated in udaf/ids.rs instead of living with their models
- Metadata scattered across files
- No clear conceptual organization

---

## Target Directory Structure

Each UDA/f concept gets its own directory. ID types live with their models.

```
formal/
  mod.rs                        # Entry point, re-exports

  universe/                     # U (Universe)
    mod.rs
    universe.rs                 # Universe type
    universe_id.rs              # UniverseId
    universe_metadata.rs        # UniverseMetadata

  domain/                       # D (Domain)
    mod.rs
    domain.rs                   # Domain + DomainProofData
    domain_id.rs                # DomainId
    domain_metadata.rs          # DomainMetadata
    domain_set.rs               # DomainSet reference collection

  admissible_set/               # A (Admissible Set)
    mod.rs
    admissible_set.rs           # AdmissibleSet + ProofData
    spec_id.rs                  # SpecId
    spec_set.rs                 # SpecSet reference collection
    admissible_set_metadata.rs  # Metadata

  constraint/
    mod.rs
    constraint.rs               # Constraint + ConstraintKind
    constraint_metadata.rs      # ConstraintMetadata

  transform/                    # f (Transform Functions)
    mod.rs
    transform.rs                # TransformFunction + Kind + Strategy
    transform_id.rs             # TransformId
    transform_metadata.rs       # TransformMetadata

  model/                        # UDAFModel orchestrator
    mod.rs
    model.rs                    # Core UDAFModel struct + methods
    populate.rs                 # populate_from_graph logic
    serde_helpers.rs            # Serialization helpers

  metadata/                     # Shared metadata infrastructure
    mod.rs
    metadata_key.rs             # MetadataKey enum
    metadata.rs                 # Base Metadata type

  proof/                        # Proof mechanisms
    mod.rs
    types.rs                    # Proof, Property, ProofStatus, etc.
    prover.rs                   # Prover implementation
    underspec.rs                # Underspecification detection
    z3_backend.rs               # Z3 integration
```
